correctness.rationale: For unique simple real dominant root alpha with |alpha|=r>1, Binet error is O((qr)^m) and ratio |a_{m+k}|/(r^k|a_m|)=1+O(q^m), uniformly in k. Every valid append has ratio to b^t|a_m|=1+O(r^{-m}), forcing nonzero |k log r-t log b|<<max(q,r^-1)^m. Baker-Wustholz lower bounds this by a fixed inverse power of t, giving t>=exp(cm). With h=1 or 2 for positive/negative alpha, Baker separation ||j h log_b r||>>j^-D yields uniform Erdos-Turan discrepancy O(Q^{D/(D+1)}). An interval of logarithmic length delta~r^{-m} is hit at Q<=j<2Q with Q~delta^{-(D+1)}, so t<=exp(Cm). That large k makes the normalized subdominant Binet error smaller than 1/3; an interior (1/3,2/3) target interval yields an actual integer 0<d<b^t. Even k ensures signs match for negative alpha. Independent exact integer searches reproduced source-index first witnesses in 10 powers-of-two, 6 shifted-powers and 6 negative-root cases, not the asymptotics.

Kominers 2025 full primary article bounds walk length for fixed cap N and gives index thresholds for Fibonacci/Lucas, not these broad minimal-step asymptotics. The most relevant origin article full text was inaccessible despite arXiv/lawful OA attempts and an authorized institutional attempt returning vpn_disconnected; this is an explicit residual risk, not a scientific failure.
